name: Urachal Diverticulum

criteria.description: Radiologic identification of a blind-ending diverticulum arising from the anterior dome of the bladder
Recurrent urinary tract infections or suprapubic discomfort suggestive of urachal anomaly
Endoscopic visualization of the diverticular opening in the bladder dome
Exclusion of other bladder diverticula or fistulas by clinical and imaging studies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging confirmation plus cystoscopic visualization and exclusion of other pathologies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiologic and endoscopic; biopsy may be required if malignancy is suspected.

laboratory: Urinalysis showing pyuria and bacteriuria during infection
imaging: Ultrasound showing cystic structure anterior to bladder dome
CT scan delineating diverticulum anatomy and excluding malignancy
other: Cystoscopy revealing diverticular orifice at bladder dome
Histopathology if biopsy performed to exclude malignancy

distinguishingFeatures: Bladder diverticula arise from bladder wall, not urachal remnant
Typically located lateral or posterior bladder wall
Located along midline but associated with small bowel
May present with umbilical discharge but no bladder communication

redFlags: Signs of acute abdomen suggesting diverticulum rupture
references: Ashley RA, Inman BA, Routh JC, et al. Urachal anomalies: a longitudinal study of urachal remnants in children and adults. J Urol. 2007;178(4 Pt 2):1615-1618.
Siefker-Radtke AO. Urachal carcinoma: surgical and chemotherapeutic options. Expert Rev Anticancer Ther. 2006;6(12):1715-1721.
Parada Villavicencio C, et al. Imaging of urachal anomalies and their complications. Radiographics. 2016;36(2):440-454.
